widgets_values:
CHUNKED LONG-FORM GENERATION — wave 14's recipe, automated

This is the path that produced a 57.6s take with no hard cuts in any
link and no join above 3 sigma (096, 2026-08-11). What is new here is
that it runs in ONE queue instead of four hand-wired links, and each
chunk gets its OWN clause.

HOW CONTINUITY IS CARRIED — two things, and they do different jobs:

  keyframe  the previous chunk's last DECODED FRAME. Pixel, never
            latent. Feeding the last LATENT frame into the keyframe slot
            roughly doubles error per link (wave 8a arm B): the video VAE
            is temporal, so its final latent frame carries ~4 pixel
            frames of motion plus conv state, where the slot expects a
            single-image encode.

  context   the previous chunk's TAIL. A still frame carries pose but
            NOT velocity — keyframe-only chains eroded motion -19%
            monotonically, where context-fed links held flat.

PROMPTS: one clause per line in H3 Long-form Links, one clause per
chunk. HEAD and TAIL repeat verbatim; only the clause changes. Wire
chunk_count into expected_count or a mismatch silently repeats the last
clause instead of erroring.

context_frames 39 lands exactly on the audio grid. Wave 14 used 22,
which is the worst legal value (36.667 audio steps) — a free improvement
to a proven recipe.

widgets_values:
SEPARATE SHOTS — 4 x 10s, cut between

The shot list drives total_frames and cut_frames. Each row is
SECONDS | framing | action. Ten seconds becomes 243 frames because
240 is not a legal run (17n+5), and it says so in its info.

EVERY ROW MUST BE A DIFFERENT SETUP. A cut between two identical
framings is a jump cut, not an edit, and that is the one thing
this node cannot check for you. The rows here change angle and
distance deliberately.

A chunk that STARTS a shot carries pin 0 — no inherited prefix, no
motion context, a clean break. So the contrast carry measured at
+12/+7/+5% per chunk resets at every cut and never accumulates.

That is the trade: cuts you have to actually mean, in exchange for
no drift and no seam to hide.

chunk_mode IS `scene` HERE

`scene` normally finds cuts by differencing a SOURCE clip, which
generating from nothing cannot do. cut_frames is how a T2V take
gets shot boundaries at all.

Four shots of one chunk each means four clauses. A shot LONGER
than chunk_frames splits into several chunks and needs a clause
each — the shot list's info output tells you how many.

DIALOGUE — lines in, timed beats out

SPEAKER | verb | text, one per line. A BLANK LINE forces a break to
the next chunk; otherwise lines fill each chunk in order.

It will never place a line inside the pin. The first 22 frames of a
chunk are reproduced from the previous one, so speech scheduled there
is simply never said — a failure that stays invisible until a render
finishes.

`pacing: spread` lays a chunk's lines across its whole window instead
of crowding them into the first two seconds. Read the LINT: it reports
silence across a seam, which is a floor set by the pin and can only be
placed, never removed.
